 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .8,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 27.04.2021 at about 8.00 a.m., when he was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-44-W-9925 on Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 Road, Nelamangala Taluk, when he reached near Dabaspete Fly Over, at that time all of a sudden a Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-04-AM-7632 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle.

Due to which, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to Government Hospital, Dabaspete and then shifted to NIMHANS Hospital and later shifted to SSM Hospital, Hassan, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as a Sales Executive and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry by its driver.
The respondents being insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, the respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate Written Statement.
In the written statement of respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
He also denied age, occupation and income of injured.
He has also denied the place, time and manner of accident.
The petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further this respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in the name of 2nd respondent and same is valid from 19.06.2020 to 18.06.2021 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further contended that the petitioner himself was responsible and he was riding the said motor cycle without observing the moving vehicle on road and was driven at high speed without following traffic rules and also he did not possess a valid and effective driving license to drive the said class of vehicle on the date of accident.
Further the driver of lorry was not at all responsible and said vehicle was not involved in the accident in any manner.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent in his written statement has contended that the lorry was insured with the United India Insurance Vide (Policy No.0102023120P102680374 valid from 19.06.2020 to 18.06.2021.

Further contended on 16.10.2014, the driver of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-04-AM-7632 belonging to 2nd respondent was driven by its driver very carefully and cautiously following all traffic rules in a slow manner and when he reached near Dabaspet Fly over, petitioner was trying to cross the road without following the traffic rules and without observing the vehicles moving on road,
the driver of vehicle tried to avoid the petitioner and applied break, but unable to avoid petitioner as other vehicles were also moving in said road and dashed the petitioner, due to which petitioner fell on road and sustained grievous injuries.
Further the accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent act of the petitioner.

Further the said accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry, the 2 nd respondent has duly insured the vehicle involved in accident with 1 st respondent vide Policy No.0102023120P102680374 valid from 19.06.2020 to 18.06.2021.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 27.04.2021 at about 08.00 a.m., on Bengaluru-Tumakuru NH-48, near Dabaspete, Bengaluru, when he was riding a Motor Cycle registration No.KA-44-W-9925, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-04-AM-7632 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and the petitioner examined Sri.Jayakumar, Medical Record Room Maintenance of SSM Multi Speciality Hospital, Hassan examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 and closed his side of evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent Insurance Company examined its A.O as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & 2 and closed her side of evidence.
7. I have heard the arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record.

8. Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:-
Mr.Pradeep.B.D vs United India Insurance Co on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103619987/
3  -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner has contended that on 27.04.2021 at about 08.00 a.m., On Bengaluru - Tumkuru NH- 48, Near, Dabaspete, Bengaluru, he met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-04- AM-7632 by its driver and he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-04-AM-7632 by its driver, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
In his chief examination he has deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.
11. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 & 2 - FIR & first information.

As per Ex.P.2 - first information was lodged by one of his friend by name Sri.Suresh.E,
S/o.Eranna on 30.04.2021, the accident occurred on 27.04.2021, so there was 3 days delay in lodging complaint.
After registering the case Police went near place of accident and drew up sketch & Spot Panchanama as per Ex.P.4 & 5 by narrating the place of accident.
As per sketch, the accident occurred on Bengaluru-Tumakuru National Highway.
Further on perusal of sketch the accident occurred on edge of National Highway.
Ex. P.6 - Vehicle Seizure Mahazar.
Ex . P.7

& 8 IMV Reports,
wherein mentioned the damages caused to both the vehicle.
Ex. P.9
- Wound certificate, it shows that petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

After completion of investigation, the police have filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.10 against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act.
12.

The respondent No.1 Insurance Company vehemently argued that there was delay in lodging first information with the police and petitioner colluding with the owner of vehicle falsely implicated offending lorry and said offending vehicle did not involve in the accident.
The respondent Insurance Company in order to prove their contention, the Insurance Company examined one Smt.Sowmya Shree.R working as Administrative Officer as RW.1.

She has deposed in her chief examination that complainant lodged first information with the police after lapse of three days and it clearly shows that the petitioner colluding with the concern police filed false charge sheet against the driver of lorry and the said vehicle not involved in the accident.

Except the oral contention taken by respondent Insurance Company, the respondent Insurance Company did not place any materials before the tribunal to established that the offending vehicle did not involve in the accident.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal and filed his objections.
In his objections, he has stated that the accident occurred only due to negligence of petitioner and there was no negligence of his lorry driver.
The respondent No.2 except filing written statement, he has not examined before the tribunal.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information lodged by one Sri.Suresh.E has stated that he has witnessed the accident and also he took the petitioner to hospital for treatment and thereafter he lodged first information with the police.
In his first information he has clearly stated the vehicle number of offending vehicle.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.17 - Case Sheet, the petitioner first went to NIMHANS Hospital on the date of accident and thereafter he went to SSM Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., for further treatment.

entities.text: SSM Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In Ex.P.17, it is mentioned that there was two wheeler on 27.04.2021 in Bengaluru exact history unknown.

Further in the same document mentioned earlier treatment Mr.Pradeep.B.D vs United India Insurance Co on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103619987/
4 taken at NIMHANS Hospital.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of record there was photo copy of Emergency Case Record for head and spine trauma of NIMHANS Hospital.
As per said document, he went to hospital on 27.04.2021.
Further in the said document history written as RTA hit by six wheeler tanker.
So, on perusal of hospital documents produced by petitioner, the petitioner went to hospital immediately after the accident with the history of RTA.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the case cannot be dismissed.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Ravi Vs. Badrinaraya in (2011) 4 SCC 693, held that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimants case.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this tribunal cannot dismiss the petition only on the ground of delay in lodging first information.
Further the respondent Insurance Company except contending that the offending vehicle not involved in the accident, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal to prove their contention.
Only on the basis of oral evidence, this tribunal cannot hold that the offending vehicle not involved in the accident.
The I.O. after thorough investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending lorry.
The respondent insurance company did not rebut all the police documents and oral evidence placed by petitioner.
Hence, the contention taken by respondent insurance company is not tenable.
On meticulous perusal of entire case the respondent did not place any material to disprove the case of petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-04-AM-7632 by its driver and petitioner sustained injuries.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.

14. The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries to right leg, right hand and head i.e., head injury with diffuse axonal injury and knee abrasion and injuries to other parts of body and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries caused to him, he has produced wound certificate issued by SSM Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., marked at Ex.P.9, wherein mentioned that petitioner sustained head injury and knee abrasion, the doctor has opined that injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

entities.text: SSM Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner also produced Ex.P.15 - Discharge Summary issued by SSM Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., wherein doctor diagnosed that petitioner has sustained head injury with diffuse axonal injury, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 28.04.2021 to 07.05.2021 i.e., for a period of 10 days.

entities.text: SSM Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In order to prove disability, the petitioner has not produced any disability certificate or not examined the doctor to show that he has permanent disability.
The petitioner has produced 21 medical bills for Rs.63,766.11/- marked at Ex.P.12 and one medical prescription marked at Ex.P.13 and two advance receipts marked at Ex.P.14.

The petitioner also examined one Sri.Jayakumar, the Medical Record Room Maintenance at SSM Multi Speciality Hospital, Hassan as PW.2 and he has produced authorization letter and case sheet marked at Ex.P.16 & 17.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove his disability.

So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income Mr.Pradeep.B.D vs United India Insurance Co on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103619987/
5 and other heads.

sentences.text:
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .1,25,000/-.
15.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-04-AM-7632 by its driver.
The police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation amount of .1,25,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Twenty Five Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Mr.Pradeep.B.D vs United India Insurance Co on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103619987/
6 Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

Draw up award accordingly.
